claims.text: A nine-year-old male, previously asymptomatic, presented to the emergency department with a headache that had persisted for one month and no other symptoms. Examination showed severe short stature, Tanner stage I, no goitre and no neurological findings, and laboratory tests including complete blood count and blood glucose were normal. Brain MRI and a dedicated sella MRI showed pituitary enlargement interpreted as a pituitary adenoma.
